clue.text: Unmatched interest, say, about detailed story

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the word's last letter cut off

parts.note: interest is one example of income, the 'say' flagging the example
a parable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A financial piece: returns on savings, relative to some well-reported tale, have no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'elaborate', but it means losing a tail, and it trims the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a match is beyond comparison, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Protected shell's opening with hardened exterior

indicators.note: the hardened word forms an exterior around the single letter

parts.note: inured means toughened or hardened, as to hardship

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A tortoise or crab is protected by the first layer of its tough shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Insured means covered against loss, a sense of protected.

clue.text: Men in leather trousers displaying rear

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cowboy ... are leather leggings worn over trousers, open at the back

explanation.surface: Men in backless leather trousers, an image from a fancy-dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaps, the cowboy's leather leg coverings, have no seat, so the wearer's rear shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps is informal British for men, and also the name of open-backed leather leggings.

parts.note: reads as an order to plant something, but describes a plant hung at Christmas that couples kiss beneath

explanation.surface: An instruction: place a plant, then kiss beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by custom: couples kiss under a sprig hung at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is the parasitic evergreen hung at Christmas, under which people traditionally kiss.

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who starts keen ends up overexcited.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the initials spell the word, and the sense describes eager excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited, which matches avid and giddy together.

clue.text: OK a meeting including sweetheart queen

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the meeting word includes the other letters

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a rendezvous with their sweetheart, a queen, is OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means satisfactory, acceptable but no better, as OK does.

clue.text: Caught going into draw for cash

indicators.note: the caught letter goes into the draw word

parts.note: to lure is to draw or entice
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught out going into a lottery draw for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Endless criticism follows head of household

indicators.note: the criticism word comes after the head word

parts.note: dome is slang for the head

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: Constant criticism directed at the head of a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' in British English means harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Household as an adjective means of the home, a synonym of domestic.

indicators.note: the planet's letters go around the ring-shaped letter

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the sun
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A planet with stripes in its orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous means marked with veins, so streaked or striped like a veined leaf.

indicators.note: the reducing word takes in the old letter

parts.note: to sap is to weaken or reduce
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Fading colours in some ancient stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone is a soft talc-rich rock used for carving.

clue.text: Line the same following carbon copy

indicators.note: the same-word comes after the others

parts.note: one can mean the same, as in all one

explanation.surface: A line repeated after a carbon copy, office talk of duplicates.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact replica, so a copy.

parts.note: reads as reviewing one's position, but stock is livestock and taking other people's is theft

explanation.surface: Advice to review one's position against everyone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is cattle: to rustle is to steal livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is stealing cattle or horses from their owners.

parts.note: to sup is to drink
ere is an old word for before
go means work or function, as in it won't go

explanation.surface: Someone who has a drink before work is showing a guilty conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' is a piece here, not an order instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian terms the superego is the moral part of the mind, roughly the conscience; hence the question mark.

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read backwards
the central letter of the seven is removed

parts.note: stopped means ceased

explanation.surface: Shops shut down without pity, then turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Depots are warehouses, places where stores are kept.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below

parts.note: P comes before Q in the alphabet
an operative is a worker, an artisan

explanation.surface: A spy-film agent backing up Q, the gadget master, or his forerunner.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is the gadget man in Bond films; here it is just the letter after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is an irregular soldier, a guerrilla fighting behind lines.

indicators.note: the statues word encloses the single letter

parts.note: statues are sculpted figures

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: Statues outside Parliament and the latest laws passed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Passing time, one in performed broadcast

parts.note: ran can mean performed, as a show ran

indicators.note: one goes inside the broadcast word

parts.note: sent can mean transmitted

explanation.surface: Time slipping by as a performance is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means fleeting or short-lived, passing quickly.

indicators.note: the about-word leads, coming first

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a stiff is slang for a corpse, and a hearse carries one

explanation.surface: A train with a hearse at the front, a stiff carriage indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiff is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise, which is to train.

indicators.note: the angrier word goes around the others

parts.note: sorer means more aggrieved or angrier
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wizard grows angrier when the Church resists him.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer practises magic, which is what a wizard does.

clue.text: Ices, or better, eating water ice

indicators.note: the words eat, holding within them, the answer

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the end of Ices, all of or, and the start of better

explanation.surface: Choosing between ices: one is better while eating a sorbet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen dessert of sweetened fruit juice, which is water ice.

indicators.note: the hard letter is dropped from the section

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: Part of a church banning hard behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel is to call off, which is to ban an event.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: learning and literature, as in a man of this kind of culture
second meaning: V and A are both characters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Culture, perhaps, to be seen at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is a London museum of art and design; here it is just two letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means literature and learning, while V and A themselves are alphabet characters.

indicators.note: a Cockney like 'Arry drops his aitches, so 'here' is spoken 'ere

parts.note: reigned means were predominant, and here becomes 'ere

explanation.surface: Harry, speaking Cockney, says reindeer once ruled this land.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so reigned 'ere comes out sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the same species as the reindeer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a herd or throng
second meaning: the past tense of drive, to control a vehicle; 'is' here joins the second definition loosely

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is past tense: drove, as in controlled a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving mass of animals or people, and drove is also the past of drive.

parts.note: taken as written
a nose is a smell or scent, as of wine

explanation.surface: The slope of a nose described in profile.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is an upward slope or climb.

parts.note: eras are times or ages

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Express, as the paper's name begins

explanation.surface: An editor deletes from The Times and the Express, two newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out, a synonym of delete.

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion means rising, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: A singer eager to be promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially in opera.

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, the answer running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of under across a into the start of toga

explanation.surface: A classical muse partly hidden under her toga.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: State again reversing English bank charge

indicators.note: the English letter and bank word are read backwards

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
a rate is a fee or charge

explanation.surface: An English bank reversing a charge, then announcing it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say again, to restate.

clue.text: She gives complaint purchasing new ham?

indicators.note: the complaint word takes in, as if buying, the new letter

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint
a ham is an over-acting performer, here female

explanation.surface: A grumble about buying new ham at the deli counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham is the theatre word for a bad, overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who donates, so she is one who gives.
